headline: The investor Michael Burry, who made his name betting against the US housing market, says stocks could peak within nine months and holds put options against the Nasdaq-100 and chip stocks.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; the article itself cautions that his positions do not prove a bigger bet.
importance_line: Individual investors who copy well-known traders are most exposed, then holders of Nasdaq and chip-stock funds; the doubt is that these are one investor's forecasts and the disclosed trades do not show how large his bet is.
summary: 24/7 Wall St., in a report carried by Yahoo Finance, says Michael Burry wrote on his Substack that he has moved almost all his bearish bets into put options, contracts that gain value when prices fall, on the Nasdaq-100 index (expiring April 2027) and a VanEck semiconductor fund (expiring June 2027), while keeping longer-dated puts on Palantir and Oracle. The article stresses that this does not show his overall bet has grown, and that a market peak nine months away could arrive after the options expire.
notes: Burry's position or firm is not given in the text, so he is described only by the article's own description (famous for his bet against the housing market). The article carries 24/7 Wall St. promotional text, which was ignored.
